summary: Feed s129_double to NDR is degraded: 9.7% TCP packet loss exceeds 1% threshold and 93.4% encrypted bytes exceeds 90% tolerance, both reducing NDR detection coverage.

findings.root_cause: SPAN/mirror oversubscription or packet broker buffer exhaustion causing random packet loss - 141 of 1452 TCP packets show gaps/retransmissions indicating the broker/SPAN is dropping under load before delivery to the tool.
findings.impact_on_tool: NDR cannot reliably reassemble TCP streams or reconstruct flows; results in missed detections, broken application identification, and false negatives due to incomplete payloads.

recommended_fix.why: Passive TAP provides lossless, line-rate copy unlike SPAN which drops when oversubscribed; eliminates the 9.7% loss and restores complete traffic to the NDR which needs full payload and both directions.

findings.root_cause: 93.4% of bytes are TLS-encrypted, above the NDR's 90% tolerance. Traffic is predominantly HTTPS/TLS 1.2-1.3 with no decryption in the visibility path, so payload is opaque.
findings.impact_on_tool: NDR is blind to payload content for most flows and limited to metadata/flow analysis only; payload-based signatures, exploit detection and full application decoding fail, significantly reducing detection coverage.

params.method: out-of-band TLS decryption with key escrow or selective decrypt policy

recommended_fix.why: Decrypting at the packet broker (or forwarding session keys) restores cleartext to the NDR which requires full payload, bringing encrypted share below 90% without violating privacy policy via selective bypass.
